content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Baton Rouge

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: The PMP® credential requires a combination of formal education and documented project-management experience. Review PMI's eligibility criteria to verify you meet the education and hours-of-project-experience requirements. Gather transcripts and project records before applying; this step prevents delays in your application review.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP® training course. You'll attend interactive sessions from anywhere, learning core project-management frameworks and exam content. Our active certified practitioners guide you through real-world scenarios and exam-style questions over the course duration.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your 35 contact hours, apply directly to PMI with your education, experience, and proof of training completion. Submit the required documentation and pay the examination fee to official PMI channels. PMI will review and approve your application before you can schedule your exam.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and instructor Q&A sessions—to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your exam through Pearson VUE at a testing center or via proctored online delivery. Bring required identification and follow all exam-day protocols to ensure a smooth test experience.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, you'll enter a three-year renewal cycle. Earn Professional Development Units (PDUs) by completing PMI-approved learning activities, volunteer work, or continuing education. Report your earned PDUs to PMI before your credential expiration to maintain your active PMP® status and professional standing.
